newsitem.title: ITALY: Banco Napoli head sees crisis over as loss halves.
newsitem.headline: Banco Napoli head sees crisis over as loss halves.

text.p: The head of struggling southern Italian bank Banco di Napoli declared a period of emergency at the institution was over after it announced it had reined in 1996 losses to almost half of record levels posted in 1995.

Banco di Napoli chairman Giuseppe Falcone, quoted in daily Corriere della Sera at the weekend after the bank announced a 1996 loss of 1.65 trillion lire ($990 million), also said the institution might break even in 1997.
"The phase of emergency for Banco di Napoli is over," the paper quoted Falcone as saying.
He expected results of restructuring undertaken in 1996 to start showing up at the end of this year. "Already in 1997 we should break even, if not with a certain profit."
The bank, which is the largest in southern Italy, clocked up record losses of 3.16 trillion lire in 1995.

The Italian Treasury then stepped in with a rescue operation which included a two-trillion lire capital increase and the setting up of a so-called bad bank to take on 12 trillion lire of its non-performing loans.
"You cannot be satisfied when you end a year with a loss of 1,651.1 billion lire. But you can be when you know the efforts made to ferry the institute to a new shore," Falcone said.

As part of the Treasury's rescue operation, it put a 60 percent stake in the southern bank up for sale and has accepted a joint bid of around 61 billion lire by state-controlled Banca Nazionale del Lavoro (BNL) and recently privatised insurer INA.
The two companies are expected to complete due diligence in the next couple of weeks.

Falcone said Banco di Napoli had undergone months of intense work "but today we are consigning a perfectly reordered bank over to the new partners, a bank ready to engage itself once more in favour of southern of Italy."
However he also said difficult economic conditions in the south had got worse and it was difficult to see stimulus coming from the economy.
Banco di Napoli announced late on Friday it made a loss of 1.65 trillion lire after capital losses and extraordinary charges totalling 1.88 trillion.
Net bad debts rose 50 percent to 5.55 trillion while doubtful loans increased 32.9 percent to 5.88 trillion.

A bank statement said that from January 1 of this year 5.47 trillion worth of the bad debts, 5.06 trillion of doubtful loans and other activities had been sold to the so-called "bad bank" for a total of 12.44 trillion as envisaged under the rescue and restructuring plan.
